dedupe_keys.name: mason fast discrete event multiagent simulation library in java george mason university

description: MASON is a Java library for building agent-based and other discrete-event multiagent simulations, designed to be fast enough for very large numbers of agents and to separate the model from its visualisation. It is developed by the Evolutionary Computation Laboratory with the Center for Social Complexity at George Mason University and a community of contributors. Coverage: generic simulation software used worldwide. Version 22 provides a model library with a schedule, continuous and grid spaces and networks, an optional suite of 2D and 3D visualisation tools, and extensions: GeoMASON adds GIS data, MASON DES adds discrete event simulation facilities, and Distributed MASON, built with the Università degli Studi di Salerno, runs models on clusters and clouds. Format and access: source code on GitHub built with Maven, with a manual and tutorials on the project website; free. Licence: mainly the Academic Free License 3.0, with a few files under other open licences. Caveats: models are written in Java code, not a graphical builder, 3D display needs Java3D and JOGL installed separately, and the project website moved to people.cs.gmu.edu. Simulation uses: building agent-based models of evacuation, emergency response, traffic and infrastructure users, including GIS-based models of cities through GeoMASON. Related records: NetLogo (platform-netlogo), Repast (platform-repast), GAMA (platform-gama) and Mesa (platform-mesa) are the other main agent-based modelling platforms.
